tasks.short: Supervise biomass plant and substation work

steps.what: Supervise biomass plant or substation operations, maintenance, repair and testing

tasks.design: The manager retains supervision and uses existing work information in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Software access does not remove site judgement or the work of operators and technicians.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supervision depends on actual equipment and staff activity.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing operational records support direction without replacing it.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising unsafe or ineffective work in changing conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The manager coordinates people and can stop inappropriate activity.

reach.learn: Biomass plant dependencies and escalation procedures

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: practical plant supervision remains human; the digest does not establish a biomass supervisory labour reduction.

assumptions: Boundary is manager supervision, excluding technician execution and scheduling counted in task 15474.

Existing planners supply instructions and the plant team provides progress during s1 after receiving direction. The manager observes conditions within s1; no free structured work-readiness flag is assumed.
Use native operational records first; existing runtime earns no saving. Zero incremental upkeep because no new tool or supervisory process is introduced.
unknowns: Supervision duties and plant operating arrangements
research_questions: Which supervisory decisions require presence at the work site?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. All supervisory work remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Conduct field inspections to assess normal and safe biomass plant operating conditions

tasks.design: The manager inspects the plant or substation directly and checks available readings in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The design does not infer safe conditions from an electronic status alone.
tasks.previous_blocker: Field conditions may be absent from existing telemetry.
tasks.enabler_now: Instrument records provide context but no demonstrated replacement for the inspection.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting conflicting signs and unexpected physical conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The manager notices context and escalates uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: Field presence and inspection responsibility stay unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate investigation of abnormal site conditions
reach.learn: Plant inspection requirements and technical escalation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: field inspection retains physical observation and judgement; no new sensor coverage is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is the manager's field inspection, not routine operator rounds or repair work.
Existing instruments produce readings; the manager captures site observations during s1. No free structured safety assessment or automated clearance is assumed.
Check native trend access first; existing runtime earns no saving. Zero incremental upkeep because no new monitoring tool is added.
unknowns: Inspection scope and existing telemetry coverage
research_questions: Which inspection findings are absent from current instrument data?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. The complete field inspection remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan biomass deliveries, ash removal and maintenance

steps.what: Plan plant activities and verify delivery, ash removal and maintenance requirements
Schedule deliveries, ash removal and maintenance into available activity slots
Resolve schedule conflicts and agree plant activity timing with responsible teams

tasks.design: Configure native planning in {OPS_SYSTEM} to propose placements using the manager's verified activity requirements and fixed capacity rules. The manager resolves trade-offs, confirms timing with teams and releases the schedule; the schedule grants no permission to perform hazardous work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated placement of deliveries and maintenance can require manual calendar reconciliation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native scheduling can compare explicit durations, capacities and time windows without selecting operational priorities.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving uncertain arrivals, changing plant needs and conflicting work requirements.
tasks.human_edge: The manager negotiates workable timing and understands operational consequences.
tasks.altitude: Less routine slot placement, with plant coordination retained.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native scheduling can propose slots from explicit constraints; the biomass activity-planning saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is activity planning and agreement, excluding physical delivery, ash handling, maintenance execution and work permits.

In s1 the manager captures activity IDs, quantities and units, locations, durations, allowable windows, priority, declared resource needs, capacity limits and source versions. Suppliers provide existing availability commitments; technical teams supply maintenance needs. All manager clarification and structured capture remains in the 35% share.

The plant records owner maintains capacity and resource definitions with 5 other-role hours per 100 focal baseline hours counted here. Missing duration, capacity or availability data stays unscheduled for manual resolution in s3; no free ready-to-work flag is assumed.

Test native planning first. Existing automatic placement has no new labour saving. Eight extra focal hours cover rule changes and additional rescheduling exceptions; external team confirmation is unchanged, with no extra data-entry demand.
unknowns: Existing scheduling capability and manual placement time
Completeness of durations, windows and resource records
research_questions: Does native scheduling reduce placement time after requirement capture and rescheduling are included?

already_counted.description: Requirements, priority decisions and structured capture
Conflict resolution, team agreement and schedule approval

incremental.description: Planning rules and extra rescheduling exceptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact activity schedule, requirement versions, resources, time windows and team recipients agreed in s3; changes void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+30=65; gross 35%, net 27% after 8 focal upkeep. Range covers existing scheduling with zero new gain through 20 points of routine placement removed minus 8 upkeep. Requirement capture and negotiation retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and manage biomass plant budgets

steps.what: Prepare biomass budget assumptions and verify cost and operating inputs
Calculate budget totals and compare actual costs with the biomass plan
Manage biomass budgets by investigating variances and approving budget proposals

tasks.design: Configure native {ERP} budgets to calculate totals from the manager's verified assumptions and source costs. The manager retains variance investigation, operational trade-offs and proposal approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated cost consolidation can require manual copying and recalculation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native budget models can reuse verified mappings and fixed formulas.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing realistic fuel and maintenance assumptions under uncertainty.
tasks.human_edge: The manager understands the reliability and operating consequences of cost choices.
tasks.altitude: Less consolidation with budget judgement unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native budget models can calculate agreed formulas; this biomass budget saving is an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is manager budget preparation and management, excluding finance's final corporate approval and spending execution.

Finance supplies existing posted costs and commitments. In s1 the manager captures period, source versions, account/cost-centre mappings, currency, fuel quantities and unit costs, maintenance allowances and calculation formulas; all capture and judgement stays in the 30% share.
Missing mappings or disputed inputs return to manual preparation and s3 investigation. Activity planning in task 15474 is a separate upstream input, counted once rather than saved again here.

Test native ERP configuration first; already automatic arithmetic earns no additional saving. Seven extra focal hours count model changes and unusual reconciliation, and 3 other-role hours count finance mapping maintenance.
unknowns: Existing budget functionality and consolidation baseline
research_questions: Can the native model reproduce the checked budget after fuel-price and volume changes?

already_counted.description: Input verification and structured budget capture

incremental.description: Budget model upkeep and extra reconciliation

approvals.approved_version: Exact biomass budget proposal, source versions, period, assumptions and planned actions checked in s3; changes void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+40=70; gross 30%, net 23% after 7 focal upkeep. Range covers existing automated budgets with no new saving through 17 points of consolidation removed minus 7 upkeep; input judgement and budget management remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The manager retains plant oversight while native scheduling and budget configuration can reduce repeated placement and arithmetic.
reach: Coordinate explicit planning constraints and cost definitions with technical and finance teams.
role.ambitious_version: More consistent planning and budgets with site judgement and all new capture work accounted for.
